findings.claim: D3's wrap error does not carry 5.3.6's text. The port raises it with luaL_error, and LuaJIT's luaL_error adds the caller's 'chunk:line: ' prefix. 5.3.6 raises it from luaM_toobig through luaG_runerror, which adds a position only when the running function is a Lua function. Here the running function is the C function str_unpack, so 5.3.6 never adds a prefix. So for any non-tail call from Lua code, ours reads 'x.lua:N: memory allocation error: block too big' and PUC reads 'memory allocation error: block too big'. This contradicts design.md D3 ('Same text as 5.3.6') and §2. No test can see it: every normaliser strips '^[^:]*:%d+: ' (conformance.lua norm, conf-extra.lua:41, packfuzz.lua:133), and the cases call through pcall(f, ...) directly, where neither VM adds a position.

findings.claim: The D5 residual is described too narrowly. The pk_str2d comment, design.md D5 and §12.5, and the RESID header of deviations.txt all say only 'a decimal exponent of 2^20 or more' differs. Of the two cited LuaJIT lines, lj_strscan.c:453 is not an exponent check. It refuses any numeral with 2^20 or more significant digits after the radix point, with no exponent written. strtod, and so 5.3.6, accepts such numerals. So a second undocumented class of string arguments is refused by our pack but accepted by PUC 5.3.6.
findings.evidence: MEASURED with probes/p2.lua (run as a background task, then stopped while PUC was still working on the 2^20-digit case). pack('<d', '0.' .. ('1'):rep(2^20)): luajit.exe gives 'bad argument #2 to '?' (number expected, got string)'; PUC gives OK 1cc7711cc771bc3f. With ('1'):rep(2^20-1), luajit.exe gives 1cc7711cc771bc3f; PUC was not re-run on it (the probe was stopped). pack('<j', '0.' .. ('0'):rep(2^20) .. '1') is also refused by ours. READ: lj_strscan.c:450-454 computes ex as minus the number of fraction digits after trailing zeros are skipped, then 'if (ex <= -STRSCAN_MAXEXP) return STRSCAN_ERROR'. That runs before any 'e'/'p' is parsed and applies to hex fractions too. Line 468 is the real exponent check.
findings.failure_scenario: string.pack('<d', s) or string.pack('j', s), where s is a decimal string with at least 1048576 significant fraction digits and no exponent. 5.3.6 packs it (to 0.111... or 0); ours raises 'number expected, got string'. This is practically harmless (a 1 MiB numeral), but the residual list claims to be complete, and the code comment cites :453 for the wrong reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the comment at oclj_strpack.c:235-238, design D5 and §12.5, and the RESID paragraph of deviations.txt to say: 'a numeral whose decimal exponent, or whose count of significant digits after the point, is 2^20 or more (lj_strscan.c:453 digits, :468 exponent)'. Optionally add a RESID case to conf-extra; it needs a ~1 MiB string, and PUC's strtod is slow on it, so keep it out of the default suite.

findings.claim: D4 picked 'not enough memory for buffer allocation' because it is 'the text 5.3.6 raises under OC's cap'. The port uses that text only for results of LJ_MAX_STR or more. Below LJ_MAX_STR, a result that exceeds the RAM cap fails inside lua_newuserdata with LUA_ERRMEM and 'not enough memory', unpositioned. 5.3.6 under a refusing allocator fails in resizebox with LUA_ERRRUN and '<pos>: not enough memory for buffer allocation'. For the over-cap case actually seen in OC, the status and text differ from 5.3.6. Separately, the port runs all argument checks before allocating, while 5.3.6 can fail on memory mid-walk before reaching a later argument error. design.md D7 and §12.5 list only memory-error 'thresholds' as a residual, not this text, status and order difference.

clean_areas: Format language, line by line beside lstrlib.c:1180-1286 (read): getnum/getnumlimit (the 214748363 digit cutoff, the [1,16] limits, '!' default 8 = offsetof cD on Win64), getoption for every option b B h H l L j J T i[n] I[n] f d n s[n] c[n] z x X, spaces and < > = !, and getdetails (X takes its alignment from the next option; X at the end of the format or before a NUL errors; Xc/X with size 0 errors; align<=1 or Kchar means no padding; the clamp to maxalign comes BEFORE the power-of-2 test; ntoalign formula). All identical apart from pk_peek's bound. A NUL inside the format ends it, as in 5.3.6.

Non-printable option text (read and measured): 5.3.6 prints <\NNN> for bytes outside 0x20-0x7e using the signed-char value cast back to unsigned, and the port prints the same, including through X (probes/p1.lua: bytes 1, 31, 127, 128, 200 and 255 are identical on both VMs).

pack (read): the nil mark is pushed after the arg-1 check and before the walk; integer/unsigned overflow checks only below 8 bytes; I9-I16 sign extension; Kchar/Kstring/Kzstr checks (memchr is the same as strlen==len, because LuaJIT strings are NUL-terminated); padding and Kpaddalign do not consume an argument. Pass 1 makes every check in 5.3.6's walk order; the only order differences are memory-related (finding port-D4-cap-text).

Two-pass memory safety (read): every write goes through pk_room, which bounds it against cap-n before writing (Kint/Kuint size, Kfloat 4/8, Kchar size with len<=size re-checked in pass 2, Kstring size+len, Kzstr len+1, x 1, padding ntoalign). The o.n!=o.cap check catches a short write. Pass 2 allocates nothing, because pass 1 already converted every number given to c/s/z to a string in place, and lua_tonumberx and lua_tolstring on a string are pure. The total is uint64 and below 2^63, so it cannot wrap. o.cap < LJ_MAX_STR = LJ_MAX_UDATA, so the (MSize) cast in lua_newuserdata is safe. The userdata sits at L->top-1 while lua_pushlstring's lj_gc_check runs (lj_api.c:638-645, 748-758), so it stays anchored. The sbuf path holds 512 bytes or fewer. No TValue pointers are held across lj_gc_check (which may move the stack); fmt and data point into anchored GC strings. D4 boundary measured: 'c2147483392' (=LJ_MAX_STR) is refused before allocation.

No user code runs mid-walk (read): lua_tolstring does not call __tostring (lj_api.c:493-510), lua_tonumberx calls no metamethods, and luaL_getmetafield is raw (lj_api.c:852-863). The only possible raise during a conversion is a memory error in pass 1, before anything is written. Note, not a defect: a __gc finalizer that runs inside an lj_gc_check could replace the format's stack slot only through debug.setlocal, and then fmt would dangle. That is the same exposure as PUC 5.3.6's str_pack, and OC's sandbox debug table has no setlocal (oc 1.12.58 machine.lua:1001-1030; getlocal returns only the name).

unpack (read and measured): 5.3.6's overflow-safe general check is kept verbatim. pos can reach ld+1 only after an unterminated z, and every later option, including a nop, then fails 'data string too short' as in 5.3.6. Kchar, Kint, Kfloat and the Kstring header are read only after pos+ntoalign+size<=ld. The s payload is read only when len<=ld-pos-size, and neither subtraction can underflow. z uses memchr bounded by ld-pos. pk_unpackint reads str[0..size-1] only. Init-position rules (0, negative, far-negative, ld+1, ld+2, INT64_MIN, strings, fractions, nan) match posrelat and the 'pos <= ld' check. luaL_checkstack(L,2) runs every iteration, and the 8000-slot residual is LuaJIT's lua_checkstack (lj_api.c:102-115). pack's own pushes (nil, udata, result, error-message slots) fit within the LUA_MINSTACK slots the VM guarantees.

packsize (read): 'format result too large' is checked before 'variable-length format', as in 5.3.6. The MAXSIZE - size arithmetic is the same and cannot wrap. Xs does not trigger variable-length, as in 5.3.6.

D1/D6 (read and measured): pk_unpackint is 5.3.6's unpackint over uint64. The int64 result (J and I8 wrap, for example ff x8 = -1) is converted with (lua_Number)int64 (cvtsi2sd, round-to-nearest-even). I9-I16 fields whose extra bytes are not a sign extension still raise '%d-byte integer does not fit into Lua Integer' (p1: 'u i16 neg nofit', 'u >I9 nofit', 'u >s9 nofit' identical to PUC).
D2 (read): l/L = 8 (PK_SZINT), which also gives 8-byte alignment under '!'. PUC Win64 differs only there.

D3 logic (read): the inputs that raise 'block too big' are exactly those for which 5.3.6's sum pos+len+size wraps, and every wrapped sum passes 5.3.6's test because pos+size<=ld. Non-wrapping over-long lengths give 'data string too short' (arg 2), and the 16-byte fit error comes first, as in 5.3.6. Only the position prefix differs (finding port-D3-position).

D5 coercion (read beside lobject.c:250-343, lvm.c:94-117 and lj_strscan.c:375-530; measured on 64 strings in probes/p1.lua for j, d and init-position, all identical except the documented 2^20-exponent residual, '0e99999999'): pk_str2int is l_str2int, with hex wrapping modulo 2^64, the decimal overflow cutoff MAXBY10/MAXLASTD+neg, and an embedded NUL failing. pk_str2d's first-of-.xXnN rule is strpbrk's. Every inf/nan spelling LuaJIT accepts contains n/N before any of '.xX', so all are refused. The 0b check mirrors LuaJIT's own whitespace/sign/0b order. LuaJIT's u/l/LL/i suffixes are refused under STRSCAN_OPT_TONUM. A NUL after the first '.xX' is refused by lj_strscan_scan ('p < pe'). pk_flt2int is mode-0 luaV_tointeger. Over-int64 decimals fall back to floats ('-9223372036854775809' packs as INT64_MIN in both). A string integer given to f/d is cast to float, so '-0' gives +0.0 as in 5.3.6.

Error texts, argument numbers and positions (measured with probes/p3.lua, non-tail calls, full messages including positions): integral size, missing size for 'c', invalid next option for X, alignment not power of 2, variable-length format, initial position out of string, data string too short, string contains zeros, string longer than given size, string length does not fit, unsigned overflow, integer overflow, no integer representation, 16-byte does not fit, invalid format option, type errors with __name (and a non-string __name ignored), method-call argument shift. All identical to PUC 5.3.6 except the documented 8000-slot residual.

API discipline (read and grep): no lua_Integer, lua_Unsigned, luaL_checkinteger, luaL_optinteger, lua_tointeger or lua_pushinteger is used, and no internal lj_* function is called. The shim's macro renames (lj52shim.h) do not reach this file's translation unit, which is LuaJIT's lib_string.c. The registration stubs in the patched lib_string.c:672-690 are trivial wrappers placed before lj_libdef.h. The target differs from port/src/lj53pack.c only by the #error guards, the size_t==uint64 assert, LJ_MAX_STR with '>=' (corrected from the prototype's '>'), the D3 two-comparison hunk and the registration removal (normalised diff in review/port/t.norm.c vs p.norm.c).

Undefined-behaviour review (read): every shift is below 64 (the Kstring shift is short-circuited for size>=8, the Kint/Kuint shifts apply only for size<8); pk_u2s avoids implementation-defined casts; the float conversions are the same as PUC's; pk_copywithendian copies by index and avoids 5.3.6's pointer to one before dest.

It then returns STRSCAN_ERROR if ex <= -STRSCAN_MAXEXP (1<<20, :66). This runs before any exponent is parsed, and before the hex '*4'. :468 is the only real exponent check. So the pk_str2d comment (target oclj_strpack.c:235-238) cites :453 for the wrong reason, and the RESID header (deviations.txt:13-15), design D5/D7 (lines 103, 105) and §12.5 (line 381) list only 'an exponent of 2^20 or more'. PUC 5.3.6 converts with strtod and accepts these numerals; I measured it. One correction to the finding: the trigger is not 'significant' digits. Leading zeros after the point count too, because the leading-zero loop at :414-425 leaves dp at the '.' and ex spans them. '0.' .. ('0'):rep(2^20) .. '1' has one significant digit and is still refused. The finding's proposed wording would therefore mis-describe its own third case. Practical impact is negligible (1 MiB numerals), so low severity is right.

findings.claim: [measured] If our side crashes partway through a run, the comparator exits 2 ('the puc run did not finish ... the reference or the generator failed') when its contract says exit 1. run-packfuzz.sh then reports 'PACKFUZZ PROVED NOTHING' (exit 2) where it should report a FAIL. The cause: at the CRASH line the loop `break`s before it reads PUC's #cov/#end lines, so pm['end'] is still nil when :181 checks it and :198 dies with 2. If our output stops right after the last case line, :99 dies with 2 as a 'desync' instead.
findings.evidence: packfuzz-cmp.lua:25 promises 'exit 1 MISMATCH, or the ours file ended early (crash)', and run-packfuzz.sh:47 promises '1 = a MISMATCH, a crash'. Synthetic pair S17 (ours file ends one case early): the comparator lists '[1] CRASH | ours output ends before case 2u' and then exits rc=2 with 'the puc run did not finish'. End-to-end test with a fake luajit.exe that runs the real one, cuts the ours file to 5000 lines and exits 139 (C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/r2/review/tests/fakebuild): 'seed 1: 2 -- lines 4999: ... MISMATCH 1', 'CRASH | ours output ends before case 2811p', 'the puc run did not finish (no #end line)', 'PACKFUZZ PROVED NOTHING', rc=2. run-packfuzz.sh:120 only sets crc=1 when crc is 0, so a nonzero exit from our side never overrides the 2.
findings.failure_scenario: A memory-safety regression in oclj_strpack.c makes luajit.exe segfault at fuzz case N > 64, after the first flush. The run is classified 'proved nothing' and the message blames the reference, so someone may rerun it as instrument flakiness. In negctl-pack.sh a crashing arm would read 'FAIL (a suite proved nothing)' rather than 'caught'. In a multi-seed campaign the crash seed counts as any2 and is reported as exit 2, not 1.
findings.suggested_fix: After the CRASH break, read the rest of fp for meta lines (for l in fp:lines() do if l:sub(1,1)=='#' then meta(l, pm) end end). Treat 'puc has a meta line, ours is at EOF' (:99) as a CRASH, not a desync. In run-packfuzz.sh, when the reference run succeeded, set crc=1 whenever orc != 0 (not only when crc is 0).

For DEV2 ids, run the PUC side with 'l' rewritten to 'i8' (packfuzz.lua's sidefmt) and require equality. Leave only RESID ids unconstrained.

findings.claim: [measured] The fuzzer gives no gated evidence for D5 (5.3.6's string-to-number rules inside pack). The default profile never generates the strings where LuaJIT and 5.3.6 disagree. The coerce profile, which does, also contains the expected-mismatch class (numbers given to c/s/z), so it always exits 1, and a D5 regression would only add a second class that nothing checks.
findings.evidence: In the default profile, hostile_arg draws only SAFE_STR (:223): decimals of at most 2^53 and small hex. COERCE_STR (:229) is used only by k_coerce (:806), which mixes in r==3, numbers given to z/s1/c20/<s4 (:812). The final negctl-pack.log shows 'LJCOERCE 1 0 PASS (caught by conf-extra)': the fuzzer is blind to that arm. My coerce run (3000 cases) printed 'MISMATCH classes (1): [155] pack | ok/ok: value 1 str vs str' and exited 1, the same as it would with D5 broken.
findings.failure_scenario: A change to pk_str2int or pk_str2d that conf-extra's 44 fixed strings happen not to cover, such as a different hex-wrap edge or a decimal just above 2^63, would be visible to the fuzzer only in coerce output that is never gated.
findings.suggested_fix: Move k_coerce's r==3 branch into its own profile (for example coerce-num), so that `coerce` is expected to exit 0 and can be run as a gate. Alternatively, let packfuzz-cmp.lua accept one declared expected class per profile and fail on any other.

findings.claim: [measured] negctl-pack.sh has no arm for several decided behaviours: D6's refusal half (I9..I16 fields whose extra bytes are not a sign extension stay refused), D6's wrapping (J/I8 of ff x8 is -1), D6's ties-to-even (ROUNDDOWN covers only the rounding direction), and D4 (see T2). The suites do catch the D6 cases, so these are gaps in the proof, not in the tests.
findings.evidence: I built review-only arms from oclj_strpack.c with negctl's method (myarms.sh). D6WIDE (line 671 luaL_error replaced by (void)L): run-pack rc=1, failing 'u i9 nofit', 'u I9 nofit', 'D s9 nofit', 'D I16 nofit', 'D i12 min bad'; fuzz 80 MISMATCH. JUNS (line 713, J/I8 pushed unsigned): rc=1, failing 'u J -1', 'u J 2^64-2', 'D I16 wrapped', 'D J 2^63'; fuzz 98 MISMATCH. TIESAWAY (line 713): rc=1, failing 'u 2^53+1' and 'DEV1 2^53+1'; fuzz 15 MISMATCH. All three are memory-safe (each computes a different value or skips a refusal).
findings.failure_scenario: If a later edit to the .expect files or the scripts drops the 'nofit' or 'J -1' cases, nothing shows that D6's halves are still protected.
findings.suggested_fix: Add D6WIDE, JUNS and TIESAWAY (the anchors above, each exactly once) and a D4 arm to negctl-pack.sh.

findings.claim: [read] PT4's stated claim, 'LUA_ERRMEM before any byte is written', cannot be observed by the check. The check passes for any implementation whose final string goes through lj52_alloc. That includes a scratch block taken outside the cap and fully written, followed by a capped lua_pushlstring that is refused. No arm or fail-first has ever made PT4 fail: round 1 stops at PT1, and all 24 arms pass PT4.
findings.evidence: The check is st == LUA_ERRMEM && msg == 'not enough memory'. That the refusal comes first is shown only by reading oclj_strpack.c:605-616 (the D4 check, then lua_newuserdata, then pass 2) together with PT3's 2.0x charge. The 'used %.2f MiB' after the refusal is printed but not asserted.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression moves the scratch to malloc and also loses the charge. PT3 would catch it (1.0x), but PT4 by itself would keep passing while its title claims something it never tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword PT4 to what it proves ('refused as LUA_ERRMEM, not D4's text, not a crash'), and assert that lj52_mem_used after the refusal is back within a small margin of base.

verdicts.reasoning: The comparator breaks out of its loop at the CRASH line (packfuzz-cmp.lua:103-111) before reading PUC's trailing #cov/#ops/#end lines. pm['end'] is therefore nil, :181 sets unfinished, and :198 exits 2 with a message that blames the reference. If ours stops right after its last case line, :99 dies with 2 as a 'desync'. run-packfuzz.sh:120 promotes only crc 0 to 1, so the 2 survives, and :129 prints PROVED NOTHING. That contradicts packfuzz-cmp.lua:25 and run-packfuzz.sh:47, which both promise exit 1 for a crash. negctl-pack.sh:123-124 would label a crashing arm 'a suite proved nothing'. The suggested fix is incomplete. packfuzz.lua:629 flushes every 64 lines, and stdio also flushes whenever its buffer fills, so a real segfault can leave a partial last line. With fewer than 4 pipes, :114 dies 2 ('unparseable'). With a cut desc, :116 dies 2 ('desync'). The two comparator edits would not cover either case.
verdicts.evidence: Measured in C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/r2/review/verify-tests/t1. A real seed-1 run (2000 cases) compared cleanly (0 MISMATCH). Then ours was cut: head -2000 gave '[1] CRASH | ours output ends before case 1014u' followed by 'packfuzz-cmp: the puc run did not finish (no #end line)', cmprc=2. head -3663 (cut right after the last case line) gave 'desync: puc has meta line '#cov ...', ours has 'nil'', cmprc=2. End to end in verify-tests/e2e: a fake luajit.exe runs the real one, keeps 2000 lines and exits 139. run-packfuzz.sh (copy) printed 'seed 1: 2 -- ... MISMATCH 1', 'CRASH | ours output ends before case 1014u', 'PACKFUZZ PROVED NOTHING', rc=2.
verdicts.better_fix: Fix the verdict in run-packfuzz.sh first. The reference run has already succeeded by :112, so after the compare write `[ "$orc" -ne 0 ] && crc=1` (drop the `[ "$crc" -eq 0 ]` guard). This alone turns every crash shape into 1: a cut at a case boundary, at EOF before the meta lines, or mid-line. Then make the comparator's message honest: (a) after the CRASH break, drain fp and run meta() on its '#' lines; (b) at :99, when lo is nil, record a CRASH instead of dying 2; (c) read ours with fo:read('L'), which works under PUC 5.3. A final line with no trailing newline, or one that cannot be parsed or desyncs only at EOF, is then a CRASH, not die(2).

verdicts.reasoning: D4 (design.md:102; oclj_strpack.c:608-609) is untested. No target file other than oclj_strpack.c contains 'buffer allocation'. Every 'c' count above 2^31 in the suites goes to packsize or unpack, and packfuzz.lua:600-607 (capc) deliberately keeps pack's 'c' at or below 2^20, because PUC would allocate. An off-by-one (`>`) is visible only at total == 0x7fffff00 exactly, which no test packs. A text change, or moving the check after lua_newuserdata, would also pass every suite. One detail of the failure scenario is wrong but does not change the finding: with D4 removed, a total above 0x7fffff00 hits lua_newuserdata's LJ_MAX_UDATA check first ('userdata length overflow', lj_api.c:752-753, lj_errmsg.h:15). Only a total of exactly 0x7fffff00 would reach the allocator and lj_str_new.
verdicts.evidence: Read: grep of 'buffer allocation' over synth/target finds only oclj_strpack.c. Large-c grep: conformance.lua:114 and conf-extra.lua:117-125 and :308 are all packsize or unpack; packfuzz.lua:833-834 and :907 likewise. Measured on synth/repo luajit.exe: pack('c2000000000c2000000000','','') -> 'not enough memory for buffer allocation'; pack('c2147483392','') -> the same; pack('c2147483391c1','','') -> the same; pack('c2000000000c2000000000','',{}) -> 'bad argument #3 ... got table'. No allocation is made in any of these. LJ_MAX_STR == LJ_MAX_UDATA == 0x7fffff00 (lj_def.h:54,56).
verdicts.better_fix: As suggested. Run PT7 under pack_test.c's 64 MiB cap so the c2147483391 case is refused by lj52_alloc and never actually allocates. The boundary case c2147483391c1 (total == 0x7fffff00) is the one that catches the `>` off-by-one and a move after lua_newuserdata: either gives LUA_ERRMEM 'not enough memory' instead of D4's LUA_ERRRUN text. Add the negctl D4 arm only together with PT7, or negctl-pack.sh will (correctly) fail.

verdicts.reasoning: run-pack.sh part 2 (:126-140) compares only the set of ids where PUC differs from the .expect file against deviations.txt. A listed line can hold any value, as long as it still differs from PUC. Part 1 compares the build with the .expect, which is circular when the .expect was refreshed from that same build. The header's 'so an .expect file cannot drift from 5.3.6 unnoticed' (:20) and 'PUC Lua 5.3.6's output with the decided deviations applied' (:14-15) therefore have no mechanism behind them for the 24 Windows (17 Linux) listed lines. I reproduced it: a refusal for DEV1 2^53+1 (which D1 forbids) and a wrong rounding for DEV1 2^53+3 both pass part 2.

For DEV2 ids, rerun the case on PUC with l/L rewritten to i8/I8 (packfuzz.lua's sidefmt). The simplest place for this is a mode in conf-extra.lua/conformance.lua under PUC that emits the deviation-applied line, so that part 2 compares whole lines and leaves only the RESID ids unconstrained.

verdicts.reasoning: The default profile's hostile_arg (packfuzz.lua:388-393) draws only SAFE_STR (:223). COERCE_STR (:229) is used only by k_coerce (:806-816), and its r==3 branch (numbers given to z/s1/c20/<s4) mismatches by design, so `coerce` always exits 1. run-packfuzz.sh:33-36 claims 'exactly one class each', but no code checks that. A D5 regression on pack of an integer option lands in the same class key, 'pack | ok/ok: value 1 str vs str', as the expected numbers-to-strings mismatch: under LJCOERCE that class grew from 155 to 360. Keep k_coerce's r==3 branch as a separate documenting profile, and drop the 'one declared class' idea: that class key collides with D5 regressions.

verdicts.reasoning: The two 'RESID exp ±2^20' rows are observable at pack's own interface. pk_str2d (oclj_strpack.c:230-255) is pack's converter. It already overrides LuaJIT's scanner for inf/nan/0b to match 5.3.6, but deliberately leaves the 2^20 exponent to lua_tonumberx. deviations.txt:11-16 files it under 'the VM, not pack', and design D7 (:105) calls it 'not deviations of pack'. Yet string.pack('<d','1e2000000') raises where 5.3.6 packs inf, and '<j' with '1e-2000000' raises where 5.3.6 packs 0. That is a third pack-level difference beyond D1 and D2, against README:24's 'the same results and the same errors'. The contract did decide it (D5/D7), so this is a labelling and documentation defect, not an undisclosed bug. A fix inside pk_str2d is feasible (huge exponent: mantissa zero gives 0, otherwise ±inf or ±0).
verdicts.evidence: Measured: PUC 5.3.6 pack('<d','1e2000000') -> true 000000000000f07f; pack('<d','1e-2000000') -> true, 8 bytes. Ours (synth/repo luajit.exe) -> 'bad argument #2 to '?' (number expected, got string)' for both. Read: oclj_strpack.c:228-255 (pk_str2d calls lua_tonumberx after its own inf/nan/0b refusals); conf-extra.lua:379-380; deviations.txt:11-16, :31-32; design.md:103, :105; README.md:24.
verdicts.better_fix: Relabel the two rows as pack-level ('RESID-scan: pack's converter uses LuaJIT's scanner, decided D5/D7'), correct D7's 'not deviations of pack' for this item, and qualify README:24. Alternatively, make pk_str2d return strtod's result when the decimal exponent is 2^20 or more: 0 when the mantissa is zero, otherwise ±inf for a positive exponent and ±0 for a negative one. Account for mantissa digit counts only when the string is over 1 MB. That would make the rows exact and move them out of deviations.txt.

findings.claim: wd-blind-spots 1g says pack's runtime is at most O(format + output), so at most O(mem cap), and calls it 'Mitigation: none needed beyond the cap. Same class as 1b and 1d'. Roadmap row 205 repeats this as 'bounded by the RAM cap like string.rep'. Both are false for time. pack scans every string it is given for an integer or float option in full, and does so in both passes. One string can be passed thousands of times, so CPU time is O(k x L) while memory and output stay O(k + L).
findings.evidence: [S] pk_walk calls pk_checkint for each integer option (oclj_strpack.c:512, :523) in pass 1 (:607) and again in pass 2 (:615). For a string argument, pk_tonum (:272) runs pk_str2int, whose whitespace loops (:206, :225) cover the whole string; a float string also goes through pk_str2d (:245-254). [M] I ran review/docs/argscan.lua on synth/repo luajit.exe. It does string.pack(('i1'):rep(k), s, s, ...) with s = (' '):rep(L)..'1'. L=1e6, k=7999: one call took 6.978 s in C for a 7999-byte output, about 3.2 MB heap. L=4e6, k=4000: 14.660 s. Time grows linearly in k (k=1000 0.816 s, k=2000 1.638 s). findings.claim: The consumers investigator measured user-visible behaviour changes that shipping pack causes on our arch. The contract, the README and roadmap targets, and the designer's summary to the user all leave them out. The main one is a Plan9k regression. Today Plan9k's msdosfs uses its bit32 fallback on our VM, because string.pack is nil. Once pack exists it switches to 5.3's path (msdosfs.lua:23). On that path, mkdir on FAT12 (mount.msdos.lua:22 always mounts FAT12) with an ODD free cluster raises 'unsigned overflow' in setFATEntry12 (msdosfs.lua:158 packs bit32.lshift(0xFFFF,4)+low as '<I2'). That happens AFTER the directory entry is written (:1087/:1095) and the cluster zeroed (:1098-1099), so the image is left with an entry whose cluster is still free in the FAT. The owner's OpenGPU in-game tests also switch paths: mesh3d.lua:111-118, u16 >= 65536 or < 0 now raises instead of wrapping; submittest.lua:103-110, NaN now packs instead of raising. The investigator also found a real bug there: the hand IEEE encoder halves subnormals.

The investigator's own result (journal, consumers findings [4](2), [5], recommendation [5]) flags these. `grep -i 'msdos|FAT12|OpenGPU|mesh3d|submittest'` over design.md and every target returns nothing about them. F13 reports only '182 pass, 0 fail', which is measured against the 5.3.6 reference, so the change from HEAD to round 2 is invisible there.

findings.claim: D6 decides two readings of the user's 'unpack ROUNDS integers above 2^53', and says it is 'Flagged for the user in the summary'. The summary flags only the I9..I16-refusal half. The other half is not flagged: unsigned 8-byte fields (I8, J, L, T) wrap to a NEGATIVE int64 as 5.3.6's lua_Integer does, so ff x8 is -1 and bit 63 alone gives -2^63. Read literally for an unsigned format, the user's text gives the nearest double of the unsigned value, about 1.8446744073709552e19. The README sentence ('an unpacked integer that needs more than 53 bits comes back as the nearest double instead of exactly') implies that too. The roadmap row 207 wording ('nearest double of 5.3.6's exact 64-bit value') is accurate; the README and the flag are not.

PUC 5.3.6: -1 and -9223372036854775808 (review/completeness/uns.lua). [read] design.md:104 D6 '(64-bit, wrapping like lua_Integer: J of ff x8 is -1) ... Flagged for the user in the summary'. The designer's final result in the journal (wf_1ec6be12-070, last entry) says only: 'One reading of your decision for you to confirm: an unpacked field wider than 64 bits (I9-I16 that doesn't fit) stays refused'. clean_areas: JIT stitching, measured on the scratch build's luajit.exe (review/completeness/jitprobe.lua). Hot loops of unpack (6 results), ('fmt'):pack/unpack through the metatable, select('#', unpack(...)), {unpack(...)} (TSETM) and pcall(unpack) with errors give identical results with the JIT on and off. Traces really stitch at the new builtins (k1 root:1 stitch:1, k5 root:1 stitch:2); the TSETM/select/pcall shapes end with a return link, and there are 0 aborts. So the build gate's claim (B2) is true, even though the gate itself does not prove it.

CHECKHOOK path, measured (hookprobe.lua; CHECKHOOK is asserted in effect by build-native.sh:745-761). The same pack/unpack loops with a count hook armed (traces exit on entry), after it is cleared, and with a hook that raises mid-loop (caught by pcall) give identical sums, with JIT on and with -joff. pack is a C function (BC_FUNCC), so no hook fires inside it and the next Lua instruction takes the hook. That is the same class as string.rep and string.find; docs-1 covers the time bound.

Time inside one C call, read: LuaJIT's decimal scanner caps significant digits at STRSCAN_MAXDIG=800 (lj_strscan.c:63, :191) and every scan is linear. pk_str2int and pk_str2d are linear. So docs-1's O(k x L) is the whole extent and nothing is superlinear.

Eris and the renumbered builtins, read. eris_lj.c persists C functions only by perms value (:1771, :1829). Its only ffid comparisons are FF_C and FF_next_N, which come before string_format (lib_base.c:77 static-asserts FF_next == FF_next_N, FFDEF(next) is lj_ffdef.h:5, string_pack is :92). Prototypes and bytecode carry no ffids. The shim and the native tests use no FF_ ids. The renumbering therefore touches no persisted state, and the hash bump refuses old blobs anyway.

OC and jnlua paths that open or copy the string library, read. ocelot-brain LuaStateFactory.scala:361-428 never touches `string` after openLibs. The kernel copies the three (build/native/kernel/machine.lua:946-948), and neither OC's GTNH machine.lua nor ocelot-brain's handles the string metatable (grep). lj52shim.h has no luaopen_string rename (:361-367 declare only requiref/coroutine/bit32/eris). OC's Java and Scala code never names the string global. PersistenceAPI's walk (PersistenceAPI.scala:34-88) names each of the three once; note that its sortWith result is discarded, so the order is lua_next order, but pack has no alias.
Dropin: the same archive, the same opener, and OC's own walk; nothing variant-specific in the new code.

Linux portability of the C, read: PK_STACKBUF is a fixed 512, not LUAL_BUFFERSIZE (8192 on glibc), so the C-stack vs userdata split is identical. PK_SZINT and MAXALIGN are 8 on both. -Wextra classes (sign-compare, implicit-fallthrough, type-limits) are not triggered. The patch script's pristine path strips CR in awk before matching, and verifies only on its LF output.
Coercion of hex floats and boundary decimals, measured (hexf.lua, 14 strings including 0x1p-1075, 2.4703282292062327e-324, 1.7976931348623159e308): byte-identical on PUC 5.3.6 and ours.
